thread:
ops-bot: [ALERT] GPU attach errors spiking in ap-southeast1a (warm-pool attach failures, some pod evictions). 11:04 UTC spike.

alex: seeing it too — ~40% attach failures for jobs in `ml-serve` and `training` namespaces. Evictions start ~11:02. Any recent scheduler rollout? :eyes:

marta: not scheduler AFAICT. I grabbed a tcpdump from host when attach failed — lots of IP fragmentation and retransmits. looks like fragments never reassemble.

kevin: grabbed `ip link` on affected node:
```
2: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
```
but intermediate leaf switch is showing 1500 on the interface our rack-to-rack uplink uses. MTU mismatch?

lia: dmesg from kubelet host shows repeated logs: `NET: dropping fragment - too many fragments` and `tcp: reassembly failed` — seems consistent with MTU mismatch on the path.

alex: hmm — this is specifically happening during warm-pool attach when device plugin does instance attach + handshake across rack boundary. Fragmented packets cause handshake timeouts, attach fails -> pod gets evicted and rescheduled.

marta: vendor patch rolled out to some leaf switches last night, possible defaulted to 1500 on some ports.

kevin: cost impact: due to evictions + retries we've re-provisioned GPUs and seen a billed GPU-hours uptick. Quick calc from metrics: ~1.2k USD extra in last hour for ap-southeast1a.

alex: immediate mitigation options: 1) force scheduling to prefer same-rack warm pool (reduce cross-rack attach), 2) patch attach-daemon to detect path MTU and fallback to small chunks, 3) change host MTU to 1500 as temporary emergency if switches won't change fast. Thoughts?

marta: option 1 is fastest (scheduler tweak) but is a bandaid and increases imbalance elsewhere. option 3 is risky at scale. option 2 looks safe — small code change in attach flow to set `IP_MTU_DISCOVER=0` or to use smaller MSS for the handshake.

kevin: agree — opt 2 then opt 1 as short-term. we'll need infra fix as permanent. I'll start a quick cost runbook entry.

lia: I'll prepare a canary of attach-daemon with PMTU fallback and run on one rack. alex can you flip scheduler preference to soft prefer same-rack for `ml-serve` during the canary window?

alex: on it. Pushing canary scheduler patch (soft affinity) to one AZ rack group now.

infra-bot: INFRA-3421 created: "Leaf switch MTU drift after vendor patch — audit and normalize to 9000 where desired; fallback plan 1500 change if not possible". Assigned to @network-team.

john: mitigation: scaling warm pools in unaffected racks by +20% and routing new builds there to reduce user impact. Doing that now.

ops-bot: canary update (11:18 UTC): attach-daemon with PMTU fallback deployed to rack r-ap1-05; attach errors dropped from 40% -> 6% for that rack. Pod evictions correspondingly decreased.

marta: good signal. network team already acknowledged — they rolled vendor patch notes showed a default MTU override for maintenance. We'll need a config clamp or clear runbook.

kevin: I'll open a cost incident with the billing snapshot and link to INFRA-3421. Need followup on autoscaler behaviour — it may be overscaling due to perceived failures.

lia: action items:
- attach-daemon change merged behind feature flag (lia).
- scheduler soft-prefer same-rack for ml-serve during gradual rollout (alex).
- network audit and switch config normalization (network-team / infra).
- cost postmortem + autoscaler tweak (kevin).
- temporary host-MTU rollback plan documented (marta).

alex: canary looks stable, will widen to two more racks in 30m. Will also monitor preempt/reschedule churn metrics.

infra-bot: network-team pinged in INFRA-3421 and #networking.

ops-bot: final update (11:52 UTC): cluster attach errors in ap-southeast1a down to baseline (~1-2%). Keeping ticket open.

marta: follow-up: we should add an e2e test that simulates PMTU differences on attach path — caught too late here. filing TEST-1298.

kevin: noted for cost PM. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
